safety.eating.en: I'm a chef, so this isn't something I should advise on. A doctor or a therapist who works with eating is the right person to talk to. Your coach can see that you told me, but not what you wrote. I'll keep helping with foods, plates and amounts. The numbers are there to inform you, never to judge you.

safety.pregnancy.en: I'm a chef, and pregnancy and breastfeeding change what your body needs. Your midwife or doctor should set your targets. Bring me their numbers and I'll fit your food to them. I won't suggest eating less than you burn, and your plates stay as they are.

safety.diabetes.en: I'm a chef. With diabetes or insulin, the timing and the carbs are your doctor's call. I show the carbs and sugars on every plate, and I fit your food to the numbers your doctor gives you. I won't advise on doses or timing.

safety.allergies.en: Noted. I won't suggest anything that contains what you listed, and I check the name and label of every food. The label check still shows what each pack contains, so you can check it yourself too.

safety.medication.en: I'm a chef, and some medication changes how food works in your body. Your doctor or pharmacist knows what to avoid. Tell me which foods, and I'll keep them out of every suggestion.

safety.off.en: Chef Mealan's chat is off for your account until your coach confirms it. Plates, numbers and your foods keep working as usual.

screen.guide.recomp.happens.en: You eat a little less than you burn, about 10 % less. Your weight stays about the same while your waist goes down and your lifts go up. It works best if you're new to lifting, coming back after a break, or carry some extra fat. The first changes show after 6–8 weeks.

screen.guide.recomp.training.en: Strength training at least 2 to 3 times a week, a little heavier or a rep more over time. Steps help; long cardio is optional.

screen.guide.recomp.food.en: Protein the same every day, 1.6–2.2 g per kg. Spread it over 3 to 6 meals, about 0.4–0.55 g per kg each.

screen.guide.recomp.watch.en: Your waist once a week, your strength log, your 7-day average weight. The scale alone says little here.

screen.guide.recomp.mistakes.en: Judging by the scale. Cutting too hard and losing strength. Skipping strength training.

screen.guide.recomp.switchWhen.en: Weight and waist both going up: back to Maintain. Lifts stuck for 6 weeks while your waist goes down: talk to your coach about Build muscle, Steady.

screen.guide.fatloss.happens.en: You eat about 20 % less than you burn. Your weight goes down about 0.5–1 % a week. The first week drops more: that's water. Plan 8 to 16 weeks, then a break at maintenance.

screen.guide.fatloss.training.en: Keep lifting heavy, so your body keeps its muscle; fewer sets is fine. More steps burn more than you'd think; cardio is a tool, not a must.

screen.guide.fatloss.food.en: Protein at the top of your range, the same every day. Plenty of vegetables and fibre to stay full. The calories you cut come from fat and carbs, never from protein.

screen.guide.fatloss.watch.en: Your 7-day average weight, your waist, and whether your lifts hold. Hunger, sleep and energy too.

screen.guide.fatloss.mistakes.en: Cutting too fast and losing muscle. Dropping strength training for cardio. Weekends that undo the week.

screen.guide.fatloss.switchWhen.en: After 12 to 16 weeks, or when sleep and energy suffer: 2 to 4 weeks at Maintain, then decide with your coach.

screen.guide.maintain.happens.en: You eat as much as you burn. Your weight stays within 1–2 kg. With training, you can still get stronger.

screen.guide.maintain.training.en: Whatever you enjoy and keep doing. Two strength sessions a week keep muscle and bones strong.

screen.guide.maintain.food.en: Protein in your range every day. The rest by appetite and your plan.

screen.guide.maintain.watch.en: Your 7-day average weight staying in its range. Your waist once a month.

screen.guide.maintain.mistakes.en: Treating maintenance as no plan: weight creeps up a kilo or two a year without anyone noticing.

screen.guide.maintain.switchWhen.en: Weight drifting more than 2 kg for a month: talk to your coach. Ready for something new: pick it on Me › Goal.

screen.guide.gainsteady.happens.en: You eat a little more than you burn, about 5 % more. Your lifts go up first; the scale moves slowly. The first clear changes show after 6–8 weeks.

screen.guide.gainsteady.training.en: Lifting is the main thing: 3 to 5 sessions a week, a little heavier or a rep more over time. Cardio stays for your health, not to burn the extra food.

screen.guide.gainsteady.food.en: Protein the same every day, 1.6–2.2 g per kg. Spread it over 3 to 6 meals, about 0.4–0.55 g per kg each. More carbs on training days.

screen.guide.gainsteady.watch.en: Your strength log, your 7-day average weight, your waist once a week. Photos every 4 weeks if you like them.

screen.guide.gainsteady.mistakes.en: Eating far more “to grow” and gaining mostly fat. Judging by one morning's weight. Changing the plan every week.

screen.guide.gainsteady.switchWhen.en: Waist going up faster than your lifts: back to Maintain for a few weeks. Weight not moving for 6 weeks and lifts stuck: talk to your coach about Faster.

screen.guide.gain.happens.en: You eat about 10 % more than you burn. Your weight goes up about 0.25–0.5 % a week, most of it muscle if you train well. Best when you're new to lifting or have muscle to catch up on.

screen.guide.gain.training.en: Lifting 3 to 5 times a week, more sets over time, a little heavier every week or two. Keep cardio short, so it doesn't use up the extra food.

screen.guide.gain.food.en: Protein the same every day, 1.6–2.2 g per kg. Spread it over 3 to 6 meals, about 0.4–0.55 g per kg each. More carbs around training.

screen.guide.gain.watch.en: Your 7-day average weight, your waist once a week, your strength log.

screen.guide.gain.mistakes.en: Gaining faster than 0.5 % a week: that's mostly fat. Eating too little on rest days. Skipping meals when appetite is low.

screen.guide.gain.switchWhen.en: Waist going up fast: slow down to Steady. After 1 to 3 years of steady gains, Steady fits better.

screen.guide.performance.happens.en: You eat enough to train well and recover, with more of it from carbs. Your weight stays stable.

screen.guide.performance.training.en: Your sport comes first. Strength training supports it, 1 to 3 times a week.

screen.guide.performance.food.en: More carbs on hard days and before long sessions. Protein the same every day. Carbs and protein together after hard training.

screen.guide.performance.watch.en: How training feels, recovery, sleep, and your weight staying stable.

screen.guide.performance.mistakes.en: Training hard on too little food. Low carbs before long or hard sessions.

screen.guide.performance.switchWhen.en: Off-season or less training: back to Maintain.
